api-request-steps.title: How does one request become a delivery estimate?

steps.label: Send the inputs
steps.text: Distance is 5 km. Weight is 2 kg.

steps.label: Check the request
steps.text: Reject a negative distance or an invalid weight.

steps.label: Return an estimate
steps.text: Give valid input to the model and return the predicted minutes.

api-request-steps.observation: Follow the request containing 5 km and 2 kg. Validation happens before the prediction.

audio-feature-steps.title: How does a recording become a model input?

steps.label: Open the recording
steps.text: Read the waveform, which is the sound signal over time.

steps.label: Measure frequencies
steps.text: Open a spectrogram or summarize the tone with MFCC features.

steps.label: Try a new tone
steps.text: Apply the same steps and check the predicted sound class.

audio-feature-steps.observation: The same recording moves from a sound wave to frequency measurements and a class estimate.

boolean-input-steps.title: How do we preserve yes, no and unknown?

steps.label: Recognize yes
steps.text: Yes, true or 1 means the value is 1.

steps.label: Recognize no
steps.text: No, false or 0 means the value is 0.

steps.label: Handle unknown
steps.text: Keep unfamiliar entries missing until the fill rule runs.

boolean-input-steps.observation: Known yes becomes 1 and known no becomes 0. Unknown remains missing until a stated rule handles it.

choose-model-setting.title: How do we choose a model setting fairly?

steps.label: Try settings
steps.text: For a decision tree, try depths 1, 2 and 3.

steps.label: Compare results
steps.text: Pick one score and use it for each candidate.

steps.label: Check the winner
steps.text: Evaluate the chosen setting on the reserved test rows.

choose-model-setting.observation: Try the same validation comparison for each setting. The final test checks the frozen choice.

convert-to-lowercase-remove-punctuation.title: What changes when we clean this message?

steps.label: A new message changes from WHERE IS MY PARCEL!!! to where is my parcel
steps.text: A new message changes from WHERE IS MY PARCEL!!! to where is my parcel.

steps.label: The model reads word counts and predicts delivery
steps.text: The model reads word counts and predicts delivery.

convert-to-lowercase-remove-punctuation.observation: Compare WHERE IS MY PARCEL!!! with where is my parcel before counting the words.

data-collection-steps.title: How can we trace a collected order back to its source?

steps.label: Bring rows in
steps.text: Read the order IDs and delivery zones.

steps.label: Keep the source
steps.text: Record the file name, origin and column types.

steps.label: Check and share
steps.text: Reopen the export. Share the fields your task needs.

data-collection-steps.observation: Keep the order ID, field meanings and collection source so an exported row can be checked.

datetime-feature-steps.title: Which useful inputs can one timestamp supply?

steps.label: Read the time
steps.text: Parse the input string as a timestamp.

steps.label: Extract fields
steps.text: 2025, month 2, day 5. Wednesday at hour 9.

steps.label: Choose inputs
steps.text: Use hour and weekday if they matter for predicting order counts.

datetime-feature-steps.observation: The supplied 2025-02-05 09:00 timestamp provides a year, month, day, weekday and hour.

duplicate-check-steps.title: Are these two records really the same order?

steps.label: Compare fields
steps.text: Look at order ID, name and the measured time.

steps.label: Confirm identity
steps.text: Matching IDs and values may be two copies of the same order.

steps.label: Review conflicts
steps.text: Different orders can share a name. Use the source to confirm.

duplicate-check-steps.observation: Similar names alone do not prove a repeated order. Compare the order identity and source.

encoding-choices-steps.title: Which representation fits this category field?

steps.label: Unordered labels
steps.text: Red, blue, green. Use a 0-or-1 column for each known color.

steps.label: Ordered labels
steps.text: Low, medium, high. Use ordered numbers such as 0, 1, 2.

steps.label: Many labels
steps.text: For many suppliers, learn target summaries from training rows.

encoding-choices-steps.observation: Unordered colours, ordered priorities and many supplier names call for different choices.

features-from-raw-data.title: How does a birth date become an age input?

steps.label: Raw input
steps.text: Birth date: 2000-10-03.

steps.label: Derived feature
steps.text: Age on 2025-04-01: 24 years.

steps.label: Reuse the rule
steps.text: Follow the same reference-date rule for each new row.

features-from-raw-data.observation: At the supplied reference date 2025-04-01, the birth date 2000-10-03 gives age 24.

image-feature-steps.title: How does a picture become model-ready numbers?

steps.label: Read the image
steps.text: Start with the color values for each pixel.

steps.label: Make the shape fit
steps.text: Resize to a fixed grid. Use grayscale when color is unnecessary.

steps.label: Give the model numbers
steps.text: Use the pixel grid or a short feature vector built from it.

image-feature-steps.observation: Apply the same image size and representation rules to training pictures and new pictures.

large-number-steps.title: Are we changing the display or changing the feature?

steps.label: Read the count
steps.text: This could be the number of page views.

steps.label: Display the number
steps.text: 1 × 10⁸ is the same count written more compactly.

steps.label: Transform for a model
steps.text: A log changes the input. Reuse the same log for new rows.

large-number-steps.observation: Scientific notation keeps the same quantity. A log changes the numeric input the model receives.

missing-values-steps.title: How can a new request use the training fill rule?

steps.label: Find the gap
steps.text: The weight is blank. The measured delivery time is present.

steps.label: Learn a fill rule
steps.text: Use a rule based on the training weights, such as their median.

steps.label: Reuse the rule
steps.text: Fill a blank on a new request using that saved rule.

missing-values-steps.observation: A missing weight is filled using the saved training rule. The measured outcome is a separate field.

monitoring-steps.title: What should we do when later model results change?

steps.label: Watch the inputs
steps.text: Are recent deliveries longer than training deliveries?

steps.label: Wait for outcomes
steps.text: Compare predictions with measured times once the trips finish.

steps.label: Decide what to do
steps.text: Inspect the bad cases and test an updated model if needed.

monitoring-steps.observation: Inspect new inputs and wait for measured outcomes before judging errors or replacing a model.

outlier-source-decision.title: What does the source tell us to do?

steps.label: Confirmed 5 kg: CORRECT
steps.text: Use the source-confirmed weight in the reviewed training copy. Keep the original record for tracing the change.

steps.label: Confirmed 90 kg: KEEP
steps.text: The unusual value is real. Keep it and check whether the intended model should handle heavy parcels.

steps.label: No usable slip: FLAG
steps.text: Ask for a source check. For this practice run, set the uncertain row aside; do not invent its true weight.

outlier-source-decision.observation: A verified 5 kg means CORRECT; a verified 90 kg means KEEP; no usable source means FLAG.

pick-model-metric.title: Which check matches the answer we need?

steps.label: A number
steps.text: For minutes, use the measured time to calculate the error.

steps.label: A category
steps.text: Count which urgent orders the model caught and which it missed.

steps.label: A ranked risk
steps.text: Use an ROC curve to explore risk thresholds.

pick-model-metric.observation: Minutes require numeric-error measures. Urgent-order decisions require counts of misses and false alarms.

problem-definition-steps.title: What useful question will the model answer?

steps.label: Ask a question
steps.text: How long will the delivery take?

steps.label: List known inputs
steps.text: Distance in km. Parcel weight in kg.

steps.label: Check the answer
steps.text: Compare predicted minutes with measured minutes.

problem-definition-steps.observation: For delivery time, name the inputs known before the trip and compare estimates with measured minutes.

reinforcement-steps.title: What feedback follows this robot move?

steps.label: Read the state
steps.text: The robot starts in cell 3.

steps.label: Take an action
steps.text: It chooses to move right.

steps.label: Get feedback
steps.text: It reaches cell 4, the goal, and earns +1.

reinforcement-steps.observation: The supplied robot starts in cell 3, moves right to cell 4 and receives the goal reward +1.

request-journey.title: How does the 4 km request become an 18-minute estimate?

steps.label: Open the CSV
steps.text: The new trip is 4 km. Its delivery time is still unknown.

steps.label: Run the lesson
steps.text: The model uses the pattern it learned from past trips.

steps.label: Read the answer
steps.text: 4 km

steps.label: 18 min
steps.text: Try a different distance and compare.

request-journey.observation: The request supplies distance, not a known new outcome. The model reuses its training pattern.

semi-supervised-steps.title: How do we check whether extra guessed labels help?

steps.label: Start with labels
steps.text: Train a first model using the known classes.

steps.label: Use unlabeled rows
steps.text: Add confident guesses as extra training labels.

steps.label: Check the change
steps.text: Compare with the original model on labeled check rows.

semi-supervised-steps.observation: Keep confirmed labels separate from model guesses and compare against a labelled independent check.

standardize-formats-steps.title: How do we make one shipment use consistent units?

steps.label: Raw shipment
steps.text: US date 01/07/2025, weight 18 lb and zone NORTH.

steps.label: Clean the fields
steps.text: Date 2025-01-07. Weight 8.16 kg. Zone north.

steps.label: Give model inputs
steps.text: Use kilograms, the weekday and a zone indicator.

standardize-formats-steps.observation: The supplied 18 lb shipment becomes about 8.16 kg; its date and zone are standardized too.

supervised-model-steps.title: How do known deliveries teach a model?

steps.label: Read completed trips
steps.text: Distance, weight and measured time.

steps.label: Teach the model
steps.text: Provide the inputs and measured answer for every training trip.

steps.label: Try a new trip
steps.text: Enter a new distance and weight and read the estimate.

supervised-model-steps.observation: Training supplies both inputs and measured minutes. A new request supplies only the available inputs.

text-cleaning-steps.title: How do the same text rules reach a new message?

steps.label: Read the text
steps.text: MY Parcel Is Late!!!

steps.label: Clean the text
steps.text: my parcel is late

steps.label: Count and predict
steps.text: parcel = 1 and late = 1. Predict a category from the counts.

text-cleaning-steps.observation: Read MY Parcel Is Late!!!, clean it, then reuse the fitted vocabulary to count known words.

train-save-test-steps.title: Which command should run after a request changes?

steps.label: Train and save
steps.text: Run the training script on completed deliveries.

steps.label: Change the request
steps.text: Enter a different distance, weight or zone in the new CSV.

steps.label: Run only the test
steps.text: Load the saved model and read its estimates.

train-save-test-steps.observation: Train and save once. After changing the request CSV, run the prediction script without retraining.

training-validation-test-steps.title: Which rows teach, choose and check?

steps.label: Training · 70
steps.text: Teach the model with these rows.

steps.label: Validation · 20
steps.text: Compare settings such as tree depth on these rows.

steps.label: Test · 10
steps.text: Check the chosen model once using these rows.

training-validation-test-steps.observation: The supplied split gives 70 rows to training, 20 to validation and 10 to the final test.

unsupervised-model-steps.title: How can we describe groups without supplied group answers?

steps.label: Read the inputs
steps.text: Age, income and spending score.

steps.label: Find groups
steps.text: Put shoppers with similar measurements near one another.

steps.label: Inspect the result
steps.text: Read the group averages before describing each group.

unsupervised-model-steps.observation: The grouping method sees shopper inputs. Inspect the resulting profiles before giving groups useful names.

video-feature-steps.title: Why must a motion model keep frames in order?

steps.label: Extract frames
steps.text: Read the video as a sequence of pictures.

steps.label: Measure each frame
steps.text: Use the same image model for every frame.

steps.label: Read the sequence
steps.text: Use the order of the frames to predict left or right.

video-feature-steps.observation: The same image representation feeds each ordered frame to the sequence model. Reversing order can reverse motion.

workbook-pipeline.title: How does a delivery question become a checked model?

steps.label: Prepare the rows
steps.text: Read past trips. Clean the inputs and set aside some rows to check.

steps.label: Teach and check
steps.text: Train with the measured times. Compare estimates with the check rows.

steps.label: Use and monitor
steps.text: Estimate new times. Let measured outcomes tell you when to investigate.

workbook-pipeline.observation: Prepare known inputs, teach and check the model, then monitor predictions after actual outcomes arrive.
